The proposed answer 992/2069 is too small: a valid construction with identical people forces a larger load, so C ≥ 248/517 > 992/2069.

**Construction.** Give every person the same weights: 44 colors with weight 31/2068 and 22 colors with weight 32/2068. These sum to (44·31 + 22·32)/2068 = (1364 + 704)/2068 = 1.

**Why the load is forced.** Suppose every color has load strictly less than 992/2068.
- On a weight-31/2068 color, n·31 < 992 gives n ≤ 31 people.
- On a weight-32/2068 color, n·32 < 992 gives n ≤ 30 people.
- The total number of people that can be placed is at most 44·31 + 22·30 = 1364 + 660 = 2024, which is less than 2025.

So some color must carry load at least 992/2068 = 248/517 ≈ 0.47969.

**Comparison.** The proposed value is 992/2069 ≈ 0.47946, which is smaller. Its own two-group example, with 43 colors at weight 31/2069 and 23 at weight 32/2069, is valid but not optimal. The solution restricted to the pairs (p, q) and missed this better integer allocation.

Since the proposed value is below a proven lower bound on C, it cannot be the smallest valid constant.

VERDICT: REJECT
